Common.description: Humans speak a language known as Common, created long ago by a scholar and traveler who has long since passed. Formed from a blend of ancient tongues, it was designed for simplicity and accessibility, allowing it to spread across continents and become the dominant language for trade, diplomacy, and governance. Though largely standardized, regional accents and subtle dialects persist, reflecting the cultural richness of humanity.

Elvish.description:
Elves speak a language known as Elvish, a melodic and intricate tongue descended from Faespeak. Over centuries, it has evolved into a distinct language used by common Elves, though those fluent in Elvish can often decipher Faespeak with effort. Elvish is cherished as a cultural cornerstone, reserved for poetry, rituals, and artistic expression, while Common is spoken out of practicality in dealings with other races.
Elves exhibit a striking variety in their physical appearances, with skin tones ranging from deep, earthy browns to pale, cloud-like shades. Their hair is often wavy, curly, or straight and comes in natural colors like black, brown, blond, and auburn, as well as more unique hues such as lime green or platinum, reflecting their magical heritage. Men may grow beards matching their head hair however clean-shaven is the typical preferred style, and baldness, though uncommon, can come from age, genetics or personal choice. Their eyes are equally diverse, spanning shades of brown, blue, green, and gray, with rarer tones like amber, silver, or even "Rain Drop," a shimmering blue often associated with mystical blessings.
Elven clothing blends elegance with practicality, crafted from silks, linens, and on the rare occasion, enchanted fabrics that are both comfortable and durable. Flowing robes and intricately embroidered tunics often feature patterns inspired by nature or celestial motifs, reflecting personal or familial significance. Jewelry is delicately wrought from silver, gold, or enchanted wood, often set with gemstones that symbolize the wearer’s magical affinities or heritage. Tattoos are rare but deeply meaningful, tied to spiritual or tribal traditions, and are made with enchanted inks that glow faintly or shift in color. These tattoos are typically specifically reserved for those who follow a religion, philosophy, tribe or guild that would require it, otherwise Elves typically do not get tattoos.

Dwarvish.description:
Dwarves speak a language known as Dwarvish, a robust and precise tongue descended from Faespeak but adapted to suit their pragmatic and direct culture. Over centuries, Dwarvish has evolved to emphasize clarity and efficiency, reflecting the no-nonsense nature of its speakers. Though it retains some melodic undertones from its Faespeak origins, it is more structured and rigid. Those fluent in Dwarvish can sometimes decipher the meanings of Faespeak phrases with careful attention. All Dwarves also speak Common, a necessary concession for trade and interaction with other races, though they often flavor it with their own idiomatic expressions and blunt humor.
Dwarves exhibit a range of physical traits shaped by their underground environments and industrious lifestyles. Their skin tones range from pale to ruddy, with a characteristic reddish tint along their noses and cheeks from years spent near forge fires. Hair is thick and often wavy, curly, or straight, coming in shades like black, brown, blond, red, auburn, gray, and white, with copper or gold hues being rarer but deeply revered. Male Dwarves take immense pride in their beards, which are carefully groomed and styled to reflect their personal and familial pride. Eyes, sharp and discerning, come in hues of brown, green, amber, or copper, with the occasional golden glint marking those with exceptional lineage or blessings.
Dwarven clothing emphasizes durability and functionality without sacrificing craftsmanship. Tunics and trousers made from sturdy fabrics are often adorned with intricate embroidery depicting family crests, guild symbols, or traditional patterns. Jewelry is highly significant, with each piece crafted to tell a story—be it a ring forged during a courtship or a necklace commemorating a great achievement. Tattoos are rare but hold deep spiritual or ancestral meaning, often depicting runes of protection or honor. Most important of all are heirlooms: weapons, jewelry, and crafted gear passed down through generations. Each Dwarf must craft a "birthright" masterpiece before bearing children, a symbol of their skill and lineage. Losing such an heirloom is considered a profound tragedy, as it severs the tangible connection to their ancestors and legacy.

Orcish / Erg’nah.description:
Orcs speak a language commonly referred to as Orcish or Erg’nah. A distant linguistic cousin to Faespeak, it has evolved to suit the Orcs' direct and robust nature, discarding much of the lyrical nuance in favor of sharp, guttural tones that convey urgency and power. Those who understand Orcish might recognize fragments of familiarity, but comprehending Faespeak requires deliberate study. Common, while not inherently part of their linguistic repertoire, is often learned out of necessity for trade, raids, or interactions with other races.
Orcs possess a wide range of skin tones, from pale red and earthy brown to deep green, black, and gray. Their hair, usually (but not strictly) straight, comes in colors such as black, brown, red, auburn, gray, or white. White or gray hair carries a stigma of shame among Orcs and is often shaved as a mark of contrition or dishonor. Baldness, on the other hand, may be a matter of genetics or a deliberate choice, reflecting an Orc’s individuality. Men frequently grow beards styled to match their hair, symbolizing maturity and pride. Their piercing eyes can be brown, green, amber, or even fiery red, with sclera shades ranging from white to ominous tones of yellow, orange, or black.
Orcish clothing is a vivid, garish display, favoring bold patterns, clashing colors, and heavy adornments that reflect their desire to stand out and command attention. Jewelry is equally extravagant, often forged from looted metals or adorned with trophies from their victories. Tattoos are integral to their culture, serving as living chronicles of an Orc's battles, honors, and life events. Orcs of importance frequently cover themselves head to toe in tattoos, creating a tapestry of personal and tribal history. In some Orcish societies, these tattoos are so revered that the skin of deceased warriors is preserved and displayed as ancestral relics, inspiring future generations to emulate their strength and glory. These practices underline the Orcs’ deep connection to their heritage, making their appearance a visual testament to their values and deeds.

Undercommon.description: Halflings speak a unique dialect known as Undercommon, a language born of necessity when they first emerged from the Fae Wilds. Legend tells of a time when these mute newcomers struck a deal with an imp or goblin to grant them a means of communication, creating a language that blends simplified common speech with infernal roots. While the story behind its creation has faded into myth, Undercommon remains an integral part of Halfling culture. Over time, it has evolved into a distinct tongue, retaining only faint echoes of its dark origins. Halflings, ever pragmatic, also learn standard Common for ease of interaction with other races, valuing its utility in trade and storytelling.

Faespeak.description: Gnomes are fluent in Faespeak, a melodic and intricate language passed down from their fae ancestors. Though deeply tied to their rituals and ceremonies, Gnomes find Faespeak too ornate for daily use, preferring the efficiency and accessibility of Common. They view Common as a charmingly simple tongue, well-suited to their practical, fast-paced lives, while reserving the more poetic Faespeak for occasions of reverence and tradition.

Traiggoblin dialect.description:
Traiggoblins speak a simplified dialect of Common, blended with Infernal, a remnant of their goblin heritage. Over time, this language has evolved into its own distinct tongue, only faintly resembling its darker origins. Most Traiggoblins are given names by their goblin parents that reflect their role or standing within the tribe. These names are often bastardized forms of Common words, such as Shimma (Shimmer), G’ffnt (Different), or Gait’un (Great One). Traiggoblins raised outside goblin societies adapt to the naming customs and languages of their surroundings, blending in as best they can.
Traiggoblins possess short, wiry frames with skin tones that range from earthy reds and browns to greens and blues, reflective of their goblin ancestry. Their sharp ears and abundant teeth are distinct markers of their lineage, while their other features often reflect their non-goblin parentage. They are often scruffy or disheveled, with hair that varies in texture and color from black and auburn to gray and white. Their odd appearance often makes them stand out, further cementing their position on the fringes of society.
In terms of clothing, Traiggoblins are opportunistic and indiscriminate. They collect whatever garments and accessories they can find, resulting in mismatched, eclectic outfits that often lack coordination but exude a certain chaotic charm. Jewelry, when they have it, is valued not for aesthetics but for ownership and the status it conveys. Tattoos are uncommon among Traiggoblins, though they may choose to get one if they believe it will make them more accepted or liked. Practical and eager to be admired, their choices in adornment often reflect their deep-seated desire for recognition and belonging.

Ahrewic.description:
Furfolk speak Ahrewic, a melodic and nuanced language that bridges the gap between animal sounds and structured speech. To the untrained ear, it may seem like growls, howls, or chirps, but its intricacy lies in its grace and the subtle shifts in tone and cadence that convey complex ideas. Non-speakers often mistake it for mere animal communication unless they’ve heard it before or make a careful observation, supported by cultural or natural knowledge. The language reflects the Furfolk’s deep connection to their natural surroundings and their strong emphasis on communal bonds.
Furfolk boast an extraordinary diversity in appearance, with physical traits mirroring a wide array of mammals. Their furs are highly varied, ranging from sleek, short coats to dense, shaggy pelts. Natural colors dominate, such as browns, grays, blacks, and whites, but striking patterns and hues like reds, golds, or mixed coats are not uncommon. Both males and females may sport manes, beards, and tufts of hair on the top of their heads, styled like other humanoids. Eye colors are equally diverse, from earthy tones of brown and amber to rarer shades like icy blue, violet, or even fiery red. Furfolk take immense pride in their furs, as they symbolize health, status, and fertility. They also practice a unique form of body modification, where dyes applied to the skin allow fur to grow in artistic patterns or unnatural colors, creating living tapestries that enhance their individuality.
Clothing among Furfolk is minimal, designed primarily for modesty, as their fur provides ample coverage for practical purposes. Even extravagant clothing is seen as an accent rather than a necessity, often used to highlight or complement their natural coats. Jewelry, while appreciated for its beauty, holds no special significance in Furfolk society, though some may covet or wear it as a personal preference. Tattoos are rare and generally lack importance, but the dyed fur technique stands as a vibrant cultural practice, enabling Furfolk to display their creativity and pride. A natural pattern or unusual fur color is highly esteemed, seen as a mark of unique beauty or lineage. Their aesthetic choices reflect their respect for nature and a deep sense of personal and communal identity.

Heiszek.description: Zizses speak Heiszek, a language that mimics the hissing of lizards but with a complexity that sets it apart. It features intricate inflections and melodic tones that add grace to their communication, making it a nuanced and expressive tongue. Non-speakers often mistake it for animalistic sounds, but those familiar with natural or cultural studies can discern its deliberate nature with a practiced ear. Zizses take pride in their language, using it for rituals, storytelling, and maintaining their cultural identity across generations.

Ak'iki.description:
Av'riahls speak Ak'iki, a language of melodic bird-song that resonates with intricate notes and rhythms, communicating meaning through its grace and precision. Often mistaken for natural bird sounds, it reflects their avian heritage and cultural sophistication. Non-speakers frequently misinterpret its nuances, though a trained ear or prior exposure can discern its complexity. For Av'riahls, Ak'iki is more than communication; it is an art form, with its tones reflecting their emotions and intentions.
Physically, Av'riahls are humanoids with bird heads, humanoid arms and legs, covered in feathers, with wings protruding from their backs. They are slender and graceful, though some exhibit fuller builds depending on their environment and lineage. Their feathers are as varied as their personalities, with hues ranging from earthy browns and forest greens to ash grays, jet blacks, fiery reds, and vibrant yellows. Males often boast more vibrant plumage compared to females, a natural adaptation for social displays and mating rituals. Their beaks vary from long and slender to short and sharp, suiting different roles within their society. Their avian eyes come in shades of yellow, green, red, orange, and brown, with sclera colors including red, black, and orange, adding to their exotic appearance. Instead of hair, soft feathers on their heads can be styled like human hairstyles, lending individuality to their diverse forms. Female Av'riahls, while curvy, lack breasts as they do not breastfeed their young.
Av'riahls prefer lightweight clothing, typically modest waist adornments, belts, or cloaks for utility, allowing freedom for flight. Their outfits balance functionality and elegance, often accented with designs inspired by wind and sky motifs. While they adore shiny jewelry and collect trinkets for personal enjoyment, these treasures are rarely worn except for special occasions. Tattoos are ineffective on their feathered forms, but they adorn themselves with vibrant paints during celebrations or war. These designs symbolize their identity, achievements, or roles, reinforcing their tradition and self-expression.

Sectah.description: Arrahsects speak Sectah, a complex language of clicks, trills, and squeaks uniquely suited to their mandible mouths and insectoid physiology. It is impossible for other races to speak Sectah without magical assistance, making communication with outsiders reliant on Common Sign Language (CSL) or expressive body language. Despite these barriers, Arrahsects make great efforts to connect with others, often employing gestures and symbolic movements to convey their thoughts with clarity and patience.

Plant communication.description:
Terrán are unique in their ability to communicate with plant life, a skill that allows them to glean information and those who have deepened their connection with nature are even able to persuade plants to perform simple tasks, to assist them in combat. While they can also speak Elvish and Common, these languages often pale in comparison to the depth of their connection with the natural world.
Terrán appearances vary dramatically based on the environment they grow up in. Some resemble humanoid forms with leafy hair, bark-like skin, and hauntingly beautiful eyes, while others may take on a more tree-like appearance, blending seamlessly with their surroundings. There are no clear distinctions of gender among Terrán, though some may develop physiques reminiscent of male or female adventurers they have observed in the past. Their vibrant eyes, in shades of yellow, green, red, orange, gold, violet, or pink, lend an ethereal quality to their already otherworldly appearance.
Terrán clothing is minimal, often composed of nature-inspired garments such as woven leaves, mossy fabrics, or vines. Many forgo clothing entirely, as their bark-like skin provides all the coverage they require, and modesty is not a concern due to their plant-like method of reproduction. Jewelry holds little significance to them beyond decoration or trade value, and it is rarely adorned. Tattoos, or "carvings," are rare and fleeting due to their regenerative capabilities, as their bark heals quickly over any alterations. Despite their short lifespan, carvings are often created as a symbolic gesture, commemorating meaningful moments or achievements.

Shroomite telepathy.description: Shroomites primarily communicate with one another through telepathy, a unique ability that fosters a deep sense of connection and community within their species. This telepathy, however, is limited to other Shroomites, meaning they must rely on traditional methods to communicate with outsiders. Some Shroomites are born with mouths, allowing them to speak Common and interact more easily with other races, though this is considered rare. Despite these limitations, their telepathic link strengthens their collective bond, making them incredibly unified and cooperative as a society.

Programmed languages.description: Manakeen are versatile communicators, able to speak any language they are programmed with upon creation. Over time, they can learn and master the languages of those around them, though their pragmatic nature may result in more mechanical delivery. This linguistic adaptability reflects their capacity to blend into societies, even if their social cues and emotional expressions lag behind.
